evals.prompt: I have a folder of notes for a coastal fantasy town: calendar rules, three factions, ten locations, and a few NPC sketches. Distill it into something Moonloom can use for a LunaTalk card without turning it into a lore dump.
evals.expected_output: Produces a source-to-play map that inventories the material, extracts player role and central tension, keeps only playable rules, delays/cuts excess lore, and hands off to blueprint or authoring.
expectations: The output inventories material by function instead of summarizing every fact.
The output defines playable promise, player role, central tension, and first-scene pressure.
The source-to-play map separates roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, state/consequence, route seeds, and XMLV3/Theme V3 opportunities.
The output explicitly delays or cuts material that does not affect play.
The handoff identifies the next Moonloom skill and missing author input, if any.

evals.prompt: Here is a giant world bible for an academy RPG. It has too many classes, houses, spells, history, and NPCs. Help me compress it before creating a role.
evals.expected_output: Compresses the world into modules, chooses one playable slice, defines state and route seeds, and protects the first scene from becoming a manual.
expectations: The output chooses one immediate playable problem rather than preserving the full world bible.
The compression uses modules such as core rule, player position, locations, factions, state, route seeds, and first scene.
The output keeps only names or mechanics that create actions, obstacles, costs, rewards, or relationship pressure.
The token plan cuts history and catalogs before agency, consequence, voice, or state.
The output routes to lunatalk-card-blueprint when more ideation is needed or lunatalk-card-author when fields are ready.

evals.prompt: I pasted a character draft with lots of backstory and private-sounding real-life details. Turn it into a public-safe original role card plan.
evals.expected_output: Distills the draft into fictional playable character mechanics, omits or fictionalizes irrelevant personal details, and avoids copying long source passages.
expectations: The output does not copy long source passages into the card plan.
The character compression focuses on desire, contradiction, boundary, player leverage, voice, turn behavior, and progression.
The output omits personal, confidential, or irrelevant details unless fictionalization is explicitly appropriate.
The plan preserves player agency and avoids deciding the player's feelings, consent, or actions.
The handoff is public-safe and does not claim special privileged provenance.
